verses.1: A man who refuses correction has a stubborn neck; suddenly he breaks, and there is no healing.
verses.2: When the righteous are numerous, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verses.3: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but one who keeps mistresses squanders his wealth.
verses.4: A king upholds the land through justice, but a man of bribes ruins it.
verses.5: A man who sows flattery over his companion spreads a net under his feet.
verses.6: In the sin of a wicked man there is a trap, but the righteous will triumph and rejoice.
verses.7: The righteous understand the judgment of the poor, but the wicked do not grasp knowledge.
verses.8: Rebels destroy a city, but wise men turn away wrath.
verses.9: A wise man judges an ignorant man, but the ignorant man rages and laughs, and finds no peace.
verses.10: Men of bloodshed hate the innocent, but the upright seek his life.
verses.11: A fool vents all his spirit, but a wise man holds it back in measure.
verses.12: A ruler who listens to a false word makes all his servants lawless.
verses.13: A creditor and a debtor meet together — the LORD sees both of them.
verses.14: A king who judges the poor with truth will establish his throne forever.
verses.15: A rod and reproof give wisdom, but a youth left uncorrected disgraces his mother.
verses.16: When lawless men multiply, so do crimes; but when the righteous are overtaken, they see it.
verses.17: Discipline your son, and he will bring you rest, and give delight to your soul.
verses.18: Without vision, the people perish; but he who keeps the teaching is blessed.
verses.19: Words will not correct a stubborn servant — even if he understands, he will not listen.
verses.20: Have you seen a man quick with words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.21: One who indulges his slave from youth will in the end find him rebellious.
verses.22: A man of anger stirs up conflict, and a man of wrath digs up sin.
verses.23: The pride of a man brings his downfall, but one of humble spirit will be upheld by glory.
verses.24: One who shares with a thief hates his own soul — if they are made to swear and will not reveal it.
verses.25: Fear of man lays a snare, but the one who trusts in the LORD is safe.
verses.26: Many seek the favor of rulers, but from the LORD comes the judgment of a man.
verses.27: The abomination of the righteous is a lawless man, and the abomination of the wicked is the path that is upright.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "makes all his servants lawless" — this reflects the idea that a corrupt ruler's influence spreads to his subordinates.
- v. 24: "if they are made to swear and will not reveal it" — this follows the Hebrew's structure, which implies a refusal to testify.
- v. 25: "Fear of man lays a snare" — "Fear of man" refers to being overly concerned with human opinion or approval, which leads to being ensnared.
